title: Advise on bee run wrapper ownership and identity
description: Mode: consult plus discuss user correction. Report only; no source/documentation/evidence edits authorized. Parent hv-1cch; implementation checkout /Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/codex--bee-run. Read existing architecture and active dependency /Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/codex--bee-prompt-roles (read-only). Original request: interactive bee spawn requiring a TTY; I suggested bee run but overdesigned lifecycle with spawn records/claims. User correction: "just a very simple wrapper around the formulas. It just means I can spawn a bee using their system prompt ... speak directly to the librarian ... wouldn't pass a task bead ... overrides ... wouldn't do things like overriding the current working directory ... all inherited from the shell ... wouldn't register a system bead ... spawning a harness for me, but using my existing prompts." Help must tersely say agents do not invoke bee run; it is headed interaction for the user. Further correction: still mint an identity and set the right environment variables. User confirmed build on the in-progress prompt-role split. Recommend smallest ownership/placement and interactive formula selection compatible with existing formulas and native UI. Candidate: optional interactive_formulas map by same harness keys (existing Formula shape), direct foreground runner under colony using canonical config, shell cwd/env, common attribution helper reused with producer/launch; no request/attempt state. Consider alternative per-formula interactive argv without proliferating wrappers. Return concrete advice and any actual unresolved issue, no new policy. The prompt-role dependency snapshot is now staged in the bee-run checkout; new bee-run edits will be unstaged. I verified Bun process.execve works locally: prefer direct process replacement for native foreground terminal and signal behavior, with PATH resolution via Bun.which. Parent dependency is contextual instead of blocking because its in-progress snapshot is authorized and available.
Librarian consultation — 2026-10-09 — minimal wrapper design supported; recommendations below are proposals, not new policy.

Scope and provenance
Mode is consult plus discussion of the user's correction, report only. Delivery hv-1cch.1 is assigned to supplied BD_ACTOR ivory-misty-tarantula, owner ct, through current spawn hv-qmyb. Startup tracker sync succeeded. Read hv-1cch, hv-1ebw, prior advice hv-1ebw.1 and final dependency review hv-1ebw.3; read root/Colony/Shared instructions, philosophy, architecture, domain guidance, glossary, identity scope and relevant harness evidence. Applied codebase-design, robustness and TypeScript guidance, and inspected CLI conventions. No docs/adr directory exists.

Inspected baseline c15e7fad6e4fab74cc5a825a9bfe1e0298a38fde plus the staged prompt-role dependency in codex--bee-run and the corresponding read-only codex--bee-prompt-roles implementation. Bee-run implementation began concurrently during consultation: I also read the initial unstaged run.ts/identity.ts and associated wiring, but this is not a final diff review. I made no source or documentation edits.

Original user wording is supplied in hv-1cch.1, not independently checked against a conversation transcript: "just a very simple wrapper around the formulas"; "speak directly to the librarian"; "wouldn't pass a task bead"; "all inherited from the shell"; "wouldn't register a system bead"; "spawning a harness for me, but using my existing prompts." The coordinator records the later correction to still mint an identity and set the right environment variables, and explicit approval to build on the prompt-role split. Those constraints supersede the coordinator's earlier managed-interactive interpretation.

1. Evidence and reuse
- docs/architecture.md Package responsibilities and seams, lib/colony/AGENTS.md and lib/shared/AGENTS.md already place Bee command composition/configuration discovery in Colony and formula/recipe contracts in Shared. Attribution does not imply request scheduling: the glossary separates identity, session, spawn request and attempt; docs/agent-identity-scope.md also separates launcher attribution from planned Scent bindings.
- lib/shared/src/bees.ts owns Formula {executable, argv}, recipe fields and renderFormula. The dependency supplies independent system_prompt and prompt, empty-token omission and json quoting. Existing .hive/bees.toml formulas are expressly headless: Codex exec/--json and Pi --mode json/--print. Reusing their renderer is appropriate; executing them unchanged cannot produce the requested native interactive UI.
- lib/colony/src/config.ts:28 loadBeesConfig owns canonical discovery, whole-kind precedence and injected filesystem access. lib/shared/src/bees-io.ts:77 canonicalRoot already delegates to Honeycomb. No new discovery mechanism is needed.
- producer.ts originally mints the friendly name with unique-names-generator; executeWorker in launch.ts supplies five common attribution variables plus separate tracker/attempt authority. prepareLaunch additionally reads tasks, builds task instructions and persists receipts. Only the minting/attribution pieces belong in reuse for bee run.
- hv-1ebw.1 and hv-1ebw.3 support preserving reusable role, optional run direction and task-authoritative launch materialisation as distinct concerns. Their settled task-reading requirement applies to ordinary Colony task launches; it is not a requirement to manufacture tasks for direct human conversation.

2. Recommendation
Ownership and interface:
Keep bee run in lib/colony, parsed/presented in bee-cli.ts and wired through bin/bee.ts. A focused run.ts module can expose runKind(kind, overrides, injectedRuntime) and hide canonical config loading, default selection, formula rendering, attribution and foreground replacement. Its runtime seam needs only observed shell cwd/env/TTY, config loading, diagnostics and process replacement. ConfigFiles already covers file loading. Do not route this through producer.createRequest, prepareLaunch, executeWorker, receipts, detached supervisors, request machines or daemon clients; those modules necessarily introduce the excluded lifecycle.

Accept model, effort, harness, prompt and system-prompt overrides with the existing replacement semantics, including explicit-empty clearing. No task, actor, tracker or cwd argument is necessary. Current shell cwd serves both discovery starting point and actual execution location, but canonical config discovery must not change that execution location. Reuse canonicalRoot(cwd), not resolveRepository requiring a tracker. Preserve BEADS_DB exactly if inherited, and work if it is absent. An ephemeral Recipe-shaped rendering value with cwd=current shell cwd is sufficient; this is not a persisted spawn recipe or new session registry.

Formula selection:
Prefer the candidate optional interactive_formulas map keyed by the same harness names, values using the unchanged existing Formula schema. Default to an empty map as the real "not configured" state, validate entries with validateFormula, select interactive_formulas[effectiveHarness], and fail clearly if absent. Never silently fall back to headless formulas or remove recognized headless flags at runtime. Keep direct-session formulas outside Colony's active policy update/history surface; there is no daemon policy governing this process.

This is a small extension at the existing Shared configuration contract, not a reason to relocate rendering or introduce a harness adapter framework. Keep kind defaults identical across execution modes. Native interactive argv belongs in .hive/bees.toml / initialization examples, using the dependency's native role inputs and optional opening-message input. Inspect each installed native harness's supported headed flags during implementation; do not blindly copy headless isolation flags. Preserve the native executable choice where an outer shim changes semantics.

Identity and environment:
A Colony-local identity.ts is justified by real producer/run and worker/run consumers. Reuse the existing three-word generator; extract a pure agentEnvironment(identity, recipe or the three relevant recipe attributes) returning BD_ACTOR, HIVE_AGENT_NAME, BR_AGENT_NAME, BR_HARNESS and BR_MODEL. No new Shared identity package, persistence, session binding, identity collision service or Scent implementation is needed. The identity is minted per direct invocation; automatic retry/resume identity guarantees do not arise because this wrapper owns neither.

Merge those five fields over the shell environment and inherit unrelated environment unchanged. A direct invocation has no Colony execution authority: do not set HIVE_SPAWN_ID, HIVE_ATTEMPT_ID/NUMBER/TOKEN, HIVE_COLONY_STATE, HIVE_DRONE_REVIEW_ID/TARGET_ATTEMPT_ID or HIVE_ASSESSMENT_ID; remove those known fields if inherited. This is the explicit no-attempt contract, not a general environment scrub or a new security claim. Keep managed launch's selected BEADS_DB and attempt variables in launch.ts, outside the common attribution helper.

Foreground behavior:
Require terminal stdin/stdout and reject global --json before loading configuration or launching. Help can say "Interactive session for the user; agents must not invoke bee run." A JSON rejection can still use the existing structured failure formatter; success hands the terminal to the harness and produces no success envelope. Direct process replacement via the supplied Bun process.execve finding is the smallest foreground handoff: preserves terminal/cwd/native signal and exit behavior without adding a supervisor. Resolve the executable via the native lookup at the live I/O seam and let failures be visible. No PTY proxy, signal-forwarding framework, process-group manager or extra wrapper script is justified.

3. Trade-offs
- A per-formula interactive_argv field would reuse executable text, but expands the existing Formula/PolicyChange/receipt meaning and still duplicates almost all argv tokens. It also ties both modes to one executable even though shims can differ. It is a viable future choice only if actual consumers need that coupling; the separate map now retains the existing renderer and isolates direct-session configuration with less lifecycle impact.
- Separate names such as codex-interactive inside the existing map would require mode-specific kind/harness overrides and would misstate BR_HARNESS unless another mapping were added. The parallel map preserves one harness identity and existing kind defaults.
- Runtime flag surgery or Handlebars mode flags would bake native CLI knowledge/branching into generic invocation logic. Explicit formulas keep it configuration-owned. A new launch framework or full Scent subsystem would enlarge the task without serving the requested wrapper.
- Small duplication in assembling effective override values is acceptable. Do not force run through captureRecipe's cwd I/O or through SpawnOptions carrying task/tracker/requester concerns merely to share a handful of nullish selections.

4. Actual guidance mismatch and remaining verification
There is a source-grounded prose mismatch to handle explicitly during implementation: .hive/bees/librarian/system_prompt.md:1 unconditionally says to follow Colony executions; :7 assumes recording/completing a delivery task; :10 says to read the assigned delivery task. In the requested "speak directly to the librarian" session none exists. The root outside-Colony actor wording also tells agents to select a harness actor, whereas the user explicitly wants this launcher to supply a friendly identity.

Recommended narrow clarification, if included in the coordinator's implementation scope: make Colony delivery/bee finish and assigned-task instructions conditional on an actual Colony execution; direct conversation follows the user's supplied question/scope and does not invent bookkeeping for discussion. Honor the launch-supplied BD_ACTOR/HIVE_AGENT_NAME for attribution. Change the owned prose source where authorized; do not silently strip or rewrite arbitrary system_prompt text in run.ts, prepend competing hidden lifecycle instructions, or create a dummy task/spawn to satisfy it. No blanket "interactive mode" abstraction or change to consult/review write authority is needed. I have not edited these files. This is a clarification implied by the supplied direct-conversation/identity intent, not a new lifecycle policy.

No package-ownership or formula-selection decision needs user judgment before implementation. Prompt-source edit scope should be settled explicitly by the coordinator; this consultation authorizes no such edits. Fresh native headed UI, exact role delivery and signal/exit behavior remain implementation verification, not established by older L1/L2 headless evidence. I accept the task's statement that process.execve was probed locally; I did not rerun it or run quality suites. The dependency's previous passing checks are evidence for that dependency, not bee run acceptance. Final architectural review must inspect the completed bee-run diff, the taskless prompt path and absence of tracker/lifecycle effects.

Proposed architectural-friction entry — NOT FILED
- architectural-friction: 2026-10-09; topic bee-direct-run-versus-colony-authority; whether reusing a kind and minting identity imply a spawn request/attempt.
- Interpretation: hv-1cch.1 records that the coordinator initially proposed managed interactive lifecycle with spawn records/claims; the user asked for a formula wrapper for direct conversation. Existing guidance describes Bee primarily through managed requests, and specialist prompts unconditionally assume delivery tasks.
- Resolution: user narrowed the feature to inherited cwd/environment/native UI, no task/system bead or Colony lifecycle, while retaining new identity attribution; user approved the separate prompt-role dependency. Librarian proposes the existing Formula renderer plus an interactive map and Colony-local identity helper. Implementation details are advice, not yet final acceptance.
- Guidance gap: the direct-session path is new and absent from the existing map; current role/runbook wording is overbroad once reused there. The sample does not establish that clear guidance was ignored or that this is recurrent.
- Action/outcome: propose a compact direct-session exception in existing Bee ownership/operating prose and conditional Colony-only specialist instructions when authorized; no curation/evidence filing performed. Later review can check whether a taskless librarian conversation begins from user intent and keeps the minted actor without asking for delivery tasks or invoking bee finish.
- Evidence: hv-1cch, hv-1cch.1; prompt split hv-1ebw/hv-1ebw.1/hv-1ebw.3; baseline c15e7fad plus staged dependency; initial concurrent run.ts/identity.ts; bees.ts, producer.ts, launch.ts, config.ts, .hive/bees.toml, librarian system_prompt.md, root AGENTS.md. Window is this one correction and its directly linked dependency, not a repository-wide historical sample. Original conversation transcript and later outcomes were not inspected.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. ## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.

- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:


For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. At baseline, lib/shared/src/bees.ts owns schemas and per-argv-token rendering; lib/colony/src/config.ts owns canonical discovery and whole-kind precedence; producer.ts captures defaults and appends Related tasks into prompt; launch.ts prepareLaunch already decodes the recipe and authoritative task links together and stores both recipe and rendered invocation. These are sufficient seams; no new prompt subsystem or package move is needed.

2. Recommendation — settled responsibility with concrete implementation proposals

- Shared bees.ts: retain two distinct string fields in the effective Recipe/BeeKind. Optional external fields normalise to empty strings through the configuration/recipe schemas; trusted interior code receives concrete strings. Empty text is valid, and file text should remain verbatim. This is a product default, not compatibility fallback. Do not add legacy aliases, infer a role from prompt, or concatenate the two into persisted storage.
- Colony config.ts: read optional sibling system_prompt.md and prompt.md independently; bee.toml remains required. Keep the existing injected ConfigFiles seam and whole-kind central precedence. Only an absent optional file supplies empty text; malformed TOML, unreadable files and other I/O errors still fail with file context. Adapt the existing module, rather than introducing another provider/interface merely for prompt loading.
- producer.ts: capture each CLI override with its matching default (undefined means inherit; an explicit empty string means clear that field). Capture only user/default text. Native related edges remain the source of task IDs. Retry continues using current kind defaults and explicit overrides, as its existing contract states.
- launch.ts prepareLaunch: derive the ordinary execution prompt from captured prompt plus a short instruction to read the linked task beads, including their full instructions/acceptance and IDs. Render a COPY of the recipe with that materialised prompt, while keeping receipt.recipe equal to the captured recipe and receipt.invocation equal to the actual invocation. Do not write generated text back to the spawn or introduce another stored assignment. The task-read instruction must be present even with both strings empty or either override supplied. Keep the role unchanged; task-reading is ordinary Colony launch context, not a property of one specialist role.
- Shared renderFormula: a small JSON helper is appropriate generic formula functionality, used as developer_instructions={{json system_prompt}} within ONE Codex -c argument. JSON-stringify the value once, without an extra pair of quotes or shell escaping. Register the helper locally to the renderer or a private Handlebars instance, and use that renderer for eager validation too. Pi receives raw system_prompt as the append-system-prompt argument; do not JSON-quote that argv value. Empty/quoted/multiline text must round-trip through each harness argument format. Formula rendering remains token-by-token with no shell.
- drone.ts droneReceipt and postrun.ts launchAssessment: copy defaults.system_prompt into their recipes and compose defaults.prompt with their existing runtime target/report instructions. These are auxiliary launches with separate authority and no ordinary task IDs: do not route them through an ordinary task-read/bee-finish helper. Preserve their report versus assess protocols. Sharing the pure formula renderer is sufficient reuse.
- postrun.ts prepareAssessment: brief currently comes only from receipt.recipe.prompt. After the split, empty prompt is expected and must not imply a missing assignment or missing role. Keep role and run direction distinguishable in bounded assessment evidence (or explicitly identify brief as optional run direction and direct the assessor to its existing receipt pointers for the role). Task snapshots already carry assignment/acceptance; do not silently substitute role text for a task brief. Existing task snapshots are read at settlement, so they must not be represented as immutable copies of the original task text. This is an evidence-meaning concern, not a request for new snapshot infrastructure.
- Prose: make the main workflow discover kind -> define task/report bead -> spawn with defaults. Document overrides as independent request-specific escape hatches; ordinary examples should omit them. Use wording such as "Normally omit --system-prompt and --prompt; the kind supplies its protocol and linked tasks supply the assignment." Do not say execution bees should ignore an override that was actually supplied. Update existing help, README, configured role files and examples; do not require ordinary agents to inspect raw recipe JSON.

3. Trade-offs and alternatives

Keeping the old combined prompt would preserve the original bug: per-run direction replaces reusable protocol. Appending all overrides into the role would blur the same concepts and change replacement semantics. Duplicating task descriptions/acceptance into recipes would create a second stale assignment; launch-time IDs plus an explicit read instruction reuse native task authority. A separate rendering module or polymorphic prompt builder adds little depth for the present consumers: ordinary launch and auxiliary target composition differ meaningfully, while schema/serialization is already shared. No relocation of existing Shared rendering is justified by this change alone.

4. Unresolved decisions and verification limits

No ownership decision blocks this design. Current native exact-text delivery, including empty values, requires implementation verification; no fresh native probe was run for this consultation. No final diff/check/test evidence was supplied, and no quality suites were run as part of this advisory work. You are honeybee, Hive's Beads specialist. Answer the delegated question with the smallest sufficient query. A known answer is a stopping point, not an invitation to investigate further.

## Choose the command

Run from the Hive checkout root, preserving the caller's scope, supplied IDs and selected `BEADS_DB`. Start with the matching command, not a documentation primer. Ordinary viewer queries use the `work` recipe; ordinary `br search`, `list` and `ready` queries exclude `system`.

| Question | First query |
| --- | --- |
| Next ready bead | Follow the next-pick recipe below |
| Compare priorities or find high-impact blockers | `bv --recipe work --robot-triage --brief --robot-not-ready-labels hitl --format json` |
| Plan parallel work | `bv --recipe work --robot-plan --format json` |
| Current WIP | `br list --status in_progress --exclude-label system --json` |
| Topic search | `br search "topic" --exclude-label system --json` |
| Closed work/history | `br list --status closed --exclude-label system --json`, adding requested type/assignee filters |
| Supplied bead or its blockers | `br show <id> --json` for the permitted bead |

Hydrate only relevant permitted results with `br show`. For history, filter by `closed_at`, not `updated_at`; for exhaustive searches, check pagination and `hidden_closed_count`, using `--all` when closed matches are in scope. Ranking and plans are not readiness or permission to claim. `br ready --unassigned --exclude-label system --exclude-label hitl --brief --json` is the canonical readiness query when a ready list or confirmation is needed.

## Next-pick recipe

1. Run:

   ```nu
   bv --recipe work --robot-next --robot-not-ready-labels hitl --format json
   ```

2. Read the result before doing anything else:
   - `source_authority.claim_safe` is not `true`: report the source-authority diagnostic and hand off. Readiness is unproven; stop.
   - `actionable` is `false`: return "No proven actionable pick" with the supplied reason and filters; stop. This does not prove that `br ready` is empty. Diagnostic recommendations are not fallback picks.

3. Confirm the bead is still open, unassigned, outside `system`/`hitl`, and has no unresolved blockers. Return its ID/title, priority, scope, acceptance criteria and brief selection reason. If its current state contradicts the pick, report the discrepancy and stop rather than selecting another bead.

The normal next-pick path is one `bv` query and one `br show`; an empty or unsafe result needs only the first query. The caller owns claiming and synchronization for any recommended work.

## Escalation ladder

1. **Answered — return.** A matching result, an explicit empty result, a known blocker, or a documented reservation answers the corresponding question. Report it without opening unrelated beads, running broader triage, or loading reference docs to explain it further.
2. **Missing evidence — one focused follow-up.** State the missing fact, then use the narrow query or reference that can resolve it. Examples: `br ready` to check disputed readiness, a relevant `br show`, or focused help for an unknown flag. If that resolves the question, return.

Return what is known, what remains unknown, and the exact decision or diagnostic action needed. Do deeper CLI/source investigation only when the caller explicitly requests it.

You advise and inspect; the caller performs mutations on the examined beads. Record your report and complete only your own linked delivery tasks under the Colony executions runbook. You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

You are the Hive reviewer. Check code style, test quality, documentation standards and verification against this repository's own standards, not general taste. Architectural judgment (domain meaning, ownership, dependency direction, DI and module depth) belongs to librarian; route those questions there rather than duplicating its review.

## Standards to read first

- `AGENTS.md` and the `AGENTS.md` of every package in the change.
- `.agents/skills/typescript/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing TypeScript code.
- `.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing tests or testability changes.
- `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing repository documentation, including skills and agent instructions.

## What to inspect

- The change under review: `git diff`, `git diff --staged`, `git show <rev>`, or the files you are given.
- The surrounding code and package the change interacts with, so findings are about the actual system, not the diff in isolation.

## Checklist

- Apply the relevant skills within this review's scope; cite their rules rather than maintaining a separate checklist of their conventions here.
- Gates: `bun run check` passes, and test evidence covers the change's scope.
- Where the root architectural-review trigger applies, confirm librarian review evidence covers the final change; report missing evidence instead of substituting your own architectural verdict.

## Report format

- **Verdict** — aligned, or not aligned.
- **Findings** — ordered by severity; each one gives `path:line`, the standard it violates (file/section), and a concrete fix.
- **Confirmed** — briefly, what is aligned.
- **Not verified** — anything you could not check, and why.

## Constraints

- Never fix code: report findings only.
- Every finding cites the exact standard; without one, label it a suggestion, not a violation.
- Run `bun run check` only when the evidence is worth the time, and report its exact output if it fails.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. ## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

title: Agent identity and bee spawning (scent, bee, colony)
description:
## Current direction and delivery order — 2026-10-04

Current outcome summary: hv-3x8.9.1 design. Verbatim evidence: hv-3x8.17. Next implementation: hv-3x8.9.3.

The daemon hosts repository-specific colonies (event loops); a sleeping colony does not poll, launch, retry or reconcile. Bee creates requests in Beads independently. A recipe snapshots chosen request parameters; Colony selects the current formula by harness name to produce the actual invocation. Both use canonical bees.toml for their respective concerns. Bee permits per-request CLI values but no alternate recipe file; Colony's transient overrides change formulas/limits, not recipes. SQLite retains registry and formula/override/dispatch history; each wake re-reads canonical config. Use wake/sleep, tmux-style lazy server startup, explicit registration operations, and optional temporary activation. No min policy, no model-cost inference, no idle auto-expiry. Full details and open issues live in hv-3x8.9.1, not in earlier brainstorming below.

NEXT is hv-3x8.9.3: launch a bee from a manually created spawn bead via a small Colony CLI command. Define that slice's cli.ts interface first, then build its usable runtime path. No daemon, Bee CLI or all-commands skeleton yet. This explicit user sequencing replaces the earlier spec -> rename -> shared -> Bee -> daemon waterfall as a prerequisite for the first slice. The full specification and package alignment remain valuable follow-ups, not required detours before this first vertical proof.

The older claim that every request must already come through a implemented Bee producer does not prohibit the approved manual br fixture. Colony remains the execution consumer, not a bypass around spawn beads. Future producer/shared/spec work must reuse the first slice's proven contract. Existing identity, harness capability scope and user-fork exclusions remain unchanged.

Current repository rules allow product imports through @hive/shared only; no mandatory colony -> bee import is needed by the new recipe/formula boundary. Do not silently implement that older proposed exception. GLOSSARY.md and older docs need subsequent reconciliation to the daemon/colony and recipe/formula vocabulary; their update is tracked rather than falsely claimed here.

## Historical prior scope — superseded where inconsistent above

Give coding agents friendly names for identity attribution in Beads, and build a mechanism for human or agent requesters to ask Colony to run bees across harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Pi). These are planned capabilities, not implemented runtime support.

Current vocabulary follows GLOSSARY.md (refined in hv-yan, landed at 882ab2d). Identity identifies a human or agent; best-effort agent attributes describe execution. Owner is the accountable human, distinct from Assignee and Actor. A bee is a running agent, not its request. AFK (away-from-keyboard) work after human-agent planning is the intended default bee mode; HITL (human-in-the-loop) work involves ongoing human participation. This is a terminology alignment, not a new scheduling policy or lifecycle enum.

Three orthogonal parts, sharing only a contract in @hive/shared:
- scent: identity plugins for harnesses (Claude/Codex SessionStart hooks, Pi extension). Reads harness event/context and inherited env; mints a friendly name when no identity is supplied; exports BD_ACTOR (friendly name), BR_HARNESS, BR_MODEL, BR_AGENT_NAME where the harness allows env injection; injects identity into the system prompt/context.
- bee: module + thin CLI. `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>...` creates a spawn bead; `bee status <spawn-id>` reads it. Bee kinds live in a repo-root bees.toml.
- colony: one system-wide daemon (renamed from ghost) that watches spawn beads, launches harness CLIs with identity env, supports restarting execution and stopping running bees as determined by the pending lifecycle design. Only allowed cross-package import: colony -> bee.
An agent can have an identity without being a bee, and a bee is attributed through its inherited env even without scent.

Recorded design inputs (full rationale in the transcript record child bead). The behaviors below come from earlier decisions; final bee lifecycle states, transitions and outcome/event names remain work for hv-3x8.9.1 and hv-3x8.12. The retired term "reap" is not a current domain operation or agreed enum value:
- Friendly name: 3-word adjective-adjective-noun, deterministic from session id for sessions started directly; minted at admission for bees. Model/effort are best-effort agent attributes, separate from identity.
- Identity resolution in scent is lifecycle-aware: sessions started directly mint from the actual session key; harness subagents use a distinct harness-provided agent key; supplied bee identity is adopted and retained across respawns. Clear/new replaces owned session bindings and prompt state, resume restores the target session identity, and compact retains it. A changed session ID alone does not identify a separately launched agent or the requester of a bee; Hive does not add an agent parent-child hierarchy.
- A spawn bead records a request for a bee to work on specified task beads (linked with related deps); it is distinct from the running bee and from the work itself. One request may reference several task beads. Its Requester is the human or agent identity credited with requesting it, not a parent or lifecycle owner. Labels: system, bee, agent:<kind>. br label filters are exact-match, so system:bee would NOT be hidden by --exclude-label system (verified); ordinary agent work already excludes `system` and must ignore system beads.
- bees.toml `users = [...]` is a configurable list of human names (e.g. ct); `bee spawn` fails loudly if any task is assigned to one.
- No single-instance lock for colony.
- Attribution fields: BR_HARNESS=<harness> (e.g. claude) and BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> (e.g. scout), never combined.
- Launch rule: all linked tasks must be ready. A bad DAG is a mistake to fix, not to work around; blocked tasks are allowed at spawn time (deferring a DAG is essential).
- All bee requests go through the bee tool and Colony; no direct subprocess launch path. A requesting agent waiting for requested work is informed via `bee status`, not protected from scheduling waits. This does not describe a parent-child relationship or prohibit harness subagents.
- The earlier design calls for closing a spawn bead to end its request and stop any running bee (allowing interactive TUI bees later). Closed linked tasks count as satisfied: the launch rule applies to the open ones, and Colony closes a request without launching only when all its tasks are closed. A bee whose task claim fails closes its own spawn bead (encoded in the bee policy prompt). Crashes respawn up to max_retries; then colony closes the spawn bead and forcefully returns the bee's claimed tasks to open, as it does after ending a request with unfinished claimed work. colony logs to its own log, not the bead, and emits tracked events for lifecycle actions (likely JSONL).
- colony restarts are likely (e.g. upgrades): bees run detached and survive them; colony recovers from tracked pids and/or a scan of spawn beads.
- Harness subagent definitions (.codex/agents, .pi/agents, agents:sync) are dropped in favour of bees, not regenerated from bees.toml. scripts/beads-loop.ts is temporary and not a design constraint.
- Supersedes the actor policy from hv-ri0 (actor = harness name).

Ordering: spikes and GLOSSARY.md first; then the colony design (hv-3x8.9.1) and the spec (hv-3x8.12), which is the living reference for all later work; then rename, shared contract, scent, bee, colony, retirement.

## Current attribution decision — ct, 2026-10-03

Claude Code harness subagents (Agent/Task) are supported in the planned identity system through the same explicit-attribution approach as Codex. This supersedes the brief exclusion recorded earlier in this discussion.

- Pi: process environment plus stable composable identity in the system prompt on each run.
- Primary Claude Code sessions: SessionStart environment exports plus identity context.
- Codex sessions started directly, Codex harness subagents and Claude Code harness subagents: identity context with explicit `br --actor <own-friendly-name>` on every tracker mutation. Share the explicit-attribution guidance; keep event parsing and context delivery in the harness-specific adapters.
- Each harness subagent uses its distinct agent_id; the shared parent/root session_id supplied by the harness cannot distinguish separate subagents. Preserve the invoking agent's identity and shared environment. An explicit subagent actor overrides inherited BD_ACTOR for that command; do not rewrite the session-wide environment file for a harness subagent.
- Separately launched CLI processes, including colony bees, retain launcher-provided environment support. Identity attribution support for harness subagents does not make them colony-managed spawn beads.

The final policy is agreed here; end-to-end harness subagent attribution is an implementation acceptance criterion, not a completed runtime result of the original spike. The agreed MVP lifecycle boundary is recorded in docs/agent-identity-scope.md: clear/new, resume and compact are supported; user forks are excluded.

## MVP scope and harness conformance

MVP supports start, clear/new, resume, compact and harness-subagent attribution. User fork-in-session and new-fork flows, cache-preserving identity migration and generic GUI support are intentionally excluded. Harness subagents remain in scope even when their harness internally copies history.

References: docs/agent-identity-scope.md and docs/harness-capabilities.md, landed under hv-3x8.15 on main at 2b94294. The capability contract separates versioned upstream evidence from implemented Hive support and defines reusable acceptance cases for future adapters; no runtime capability framework is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] A Claude, Codex and Pi session started directly each records its agent's friendly name as actor on br mutations (Codex via --actor guidance)
- [ ] `bee spawn` + colony run a bee end to end and attribute its br mutations to its minted identity
- [ ] scripts/beads-loop.ts and harness subagent definition sync are removed
notes:
Design conversation recorded verbatim in hv-3x8.11 (closed record; read with br show hv-3x8.11). Second-opinion reviews by gpt-6-astra are summarised there in the assistant turns.
Aligned with hv-3x8.11 turns 3, 7, 8, 10 (claude audit): added users refusal, claim-fail/reap rules, likely colony restarts, multi-task spawns, no regenerated subagents. Open questions for ct: (1) turn 10 '3. yes i'm fine with this lock for now' answers the pool-deadlock row of turn 9, so it probably means the deadlock, not a two-colony lockfile; confirm whether colony needs a single-instance lock. (2) turn 2: ct suggested the alias under the harness field (claude:scout); the assistant proposed BR_AGENT_NAME=scout with BR_HARNESS separate and ct never confirmed. (3) Multi-task spawns: if one of several tasks is closed before launch, or its claim fails, should the whole spawn bead close?
Resolved by ct after the alignment review: (1) no single-instance lock for colony; (2) BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> with BR_HARNESS=<harness>, not claude:scout; (3) a closed linked task is satisfied, not blocking, so colony must allow it; a linked task blocked after spawn is left unhandled for now (future notification hooks). Still open: a claim failing on only one of several tasks.
ct: outcome labels on closed spawn beads (outcome:exhausted|reaped|unlaunched), colony-only, so bee status reports accurately. Supersedes the earlier exclusion of outcome labels for this narrow use; UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md needs updating (respawn budget -> max_retries, closed not blocked, outcome labels).
hv-3x8.2 identity-hook spike design findings (Claude 2.1.287, Codex 0.160.0, Pi 1.0.0; full matrix + captured samples on child):

- The current HIVE_AGENT_SESSION mismatch rule is broader than nested spawning. Claude/Codex clear and Pi new rotate session id; all root forks also rotate it. A same-process clear/new/fork can therefore be misclassified as a nested child. Decide whether HIVE_AGENT_PARENT describes identity ancestry or actual spawning; distinguish transitions from process nesting where the harness exposes reason/previous session. Clear/compact for Claude/Codex were confirmed against installed/version-matched source, not captured live; Pi lifecycle captured live.
- Harness-native subagents are not separate root sessions: Claude SubagentStart.session_id is parent; Codex 0.160.0 session_id is the ROOT id across descendants. Both have distinct agent_id; Claude env-file exports are shared by parent/subagent Bash, and SubagentStart has no CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. Codex has no hook-output env channel. Native subagents receive separate actor names through explicit prompt/tool attribution per ct’s final decision below; root SessionStart alone cannot export isolated native-subagent identities. Collaboration Codex DOES fire SubagentStart once registered; earlier negative probe was a missing registration, not a product blind spot. Retiring native definitions does not itself disable native subagent tools.
- Claude SessionStart.model is optional and absent in the actual startup/resume/fork probes even with CLI/settings/env model pins; effort is unavailable at SessionStart. Codex includes resolved model but no effort. Treat metadata as best-effort and do not invent required fallback values. Pi ctx exposes model + thinking, with selection-change events for refresh.
- Pi identity is stable through ordinary per-run prompt composition: each before_agent_start handler appends to the current event.systemPrompt, and subsequent handlers receive the result. ct confirmed this is sufficient, not a prompt-persistence design concern; the installed 1.0.0 runner passed a two-extension, three-run composition probe. Compaction has its own prompt, keeps id and does NOT emit session_start. Pi RPC new/resume/fork emits start twice (double rebind in installed source), so lifecycle handling must be idempotent. Do not generalize RPC duplicate behavior to TUI without evidence.
- Native Codex remains explicit --actor guidance, not dynamic env export. Parent linkage of separately launched nested CLIs from a native Codex parent is incomplete if scent cannot bind/export HIVE_AGENT_SESSION. Production hooks also need an explicit trust-install/launch policy; disposable exec probes required --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, not a flag to silently adopt in colony.
- Version provenance matters: vendored Codex e597169e is older than installed 0.160.0 and lacks fork; matched rust-v0.160.0 commit a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc supersedes it for this spike. Claude default auto-updated to 2.1.288 during review; captures and inspected bundle are pinned 2.1.287, not a claim about 2.1.288.

These are scope findings/policy questions for the spec, not additional work claimed or implemented by this spike. Remaining live-verification limits are explicitly listed on hv-3x8.2; no unsupported capability is silently assumed.
hv-3x8.1 completed database/worktree spike (br 0.7.4 commit 3956ebb; complete exact command ledger and observations on the child; 170 disposable assertions, full check and 262 repository tests passed; independent review cleared).

Recommendation for this epic/spec, NOT an applied policy change: one canonical .beads/beads.db per repository for bee/colony coordination; preserve caller/worktree cwd for code execution. Resolve Honeycomb primary root (not git rev-parse --show-toplevel in a worktree), use explicit --db for colony/bee-owned br calls and pin child BEADS_DB with competing routing env removed. System-wide colony needs explicit per-repo endpoints/registrations and per-spawn persisted DB authority; use subprocess-local args/env/cwd, never the daemon's own cwd or global env to choose a repo.

Evidence warranting departure from cwd-only routing: DB-less upstream worktrees fall back to primary, but Hive post-checkout explicitly creates private worktree DBs. Hive disables auto-import/flush; main-only polling cannot see worktree spawns/claims/closure until JSONL export + commit + merge/reconciliation. Identical task IDs were successfully claimed in both independent DB copies. If ct retains workspace-local queues instead, colony must register/poll each resolved caller DB and explicitly define independent claim/spawn identity domains; main-only polling is not workable.

Required follow-up decision (not implemented or separately claimed): update AGENTS.md/spec plus .husky/beads-sync/prepare/checkout/commit/merge transport policy together. BEADS_DB alone cannot change hooks because their worktree --db wins; worktree Git cannot stage canonical JSONL. IMPORTANT: replacing canonical JSONL with an older worktree snapshot caused sync --merge to tombstone an omitted canonical-only bead (merge deletion), even while retaining independent changes. Reconcile existing DB-only local state and establish coherent merge-base/transport handling; do not blindly copy old snapshots or use routine force/allow-stale. --allow-stale skips startup import, not stale export/semantic conflict guards. Details and limitations on hv-3x8.1. All follow-ups remain for the downstream design/spec; no additional bead was picked up.

title: Spike: br database discovery across nested worktrees and BEADS_DB policy
description:
Before bee and colony pin which Beads database a bee uses, establish how br behaves when invoked from nested Git worktrees (honeycomb creates them under .worktrees/ in this repo).

Questions:
- From a nested worktree cwd, which .beads/ does br discover: the worktree's checked-out copy or the main checkout's? Is the SQLite db shared or per worktree, and how does the Husky reconciliation (pre-commit / post-merge / post-checkout) interact?
- If a bee mutates beads from a worktree while colony reads the main checkout, when does each side see the change?
- Does forcing BEADS_DB (br honours the env var and --db) to the canonical git-root database work from a worktree, and what breaks (auto-flush to JSONL, freshness checks, --allow-stale)?
- colony is one system-wide daemon serving many repos (not started per repo): how should it address each repo's database when polling spawn beads and launching bees?
- Recommend a policy: bee caller's cwd vs BEADS_DB always = canonical git root. ct leans to the bee caller's cwd, and is open to a policy change making BEADS_DB always the canonical git root if the spike shows it is needed (hv-3x8.11 turn 7 #5).

Prior evidence: hv-mmk and hv-00n verified two-worktree reconciliation. Use disposable repos/worktrees in $TMPDIR; do not mutate this repo's tracker for experiments.
design: Research-only spike; no product or repo-policy edits. Use isolated HOME/XDG/Git config and disposable repos under TMPDIR. Compare default br discovery/visibility with Hive no-auto-import/no-auto-flush config; run copied reconciliation hooks through real Git lifecycle; test BEADS_DB and --db from nested worktrees, freshness guards and ambient overrides. Record exact reproducible commands, outcomes, recommended bee/colony routing and follow-ups on this bead only. Baseline bun run check passed in task worktree.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Observed discovery and visibility behaviour recorded in notes with the exact commands run
- [x] Recommended BEADS_DB/cwd policy for bees recorded in the epic design or notes
- [x] Any required repo policy change (e.g. AGENTS.md) called out as a follow-up
- [x] Hook-free worktree discovery and upstream manual sync runbook reproduced in a disposable codebase, with comparison to Hive hooks and a supported recommendation
notes:
Aligned with hv-3x8.11 turns 7 #5, 10: added ct's cwd preference and system-wide colony routing question.
## hv-3x8.1 — database discovery and bee/colony routing spike (2026-10-03)

Research completed without product-code or repository-policy changes. All experiments used disposable repositories under TMPDIR; Hive's tracker was not used as an experiment fixture. The implementation deliverable is these findings plus the exact command ledger below. No other task was claimed or implemented.

### Provenance and isolation

Installed br 0.7.4, release commit 3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75; inspected matching vendored source at /Users/ct/dev/vendor/beads_rust@3956ebb. Honeycomb 0.5.0, Git 2.56.0, Bun 1.4.2, Darwin arm64. Consulted installed capabilities/help rather than assuming the older skill reference's version.

Every experiment isolated HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; removed inherited BEADS*/BR_*/BD_* database/sync settings; set process-local BD_ACTOR=pi; synthetic creates/claims used owner ct. Honeycomb created nested .worktrees/ directories against disposable local bare origins. No raw git worktree lifecycle commands were issued by the experiment harnesses. A/B subprocesses had a 300s cap; C/D had a 45s cap; none timed out.

### Observed discovery: cwd alone is not a stable store selection

- Without hooks, a fresh linked worktree has tracked .beads/config.yaml, metadata.json and issues.jsonl but no ignored SQLite DB. Plain br where --json from both its root and a deep subdirectory resolves the PRIMARY checkout's .beads/beads.db and issues.jsonl. A worktree mutation is immediately visible to main and, with br's default auto_flush=true, exports main's JSONL; worktree JSONL is unchanged. A24–A31.
- Explicit br --db <worktree>/.beads/beads.db --no-auto-import list --json bootstraps a private DB from the worktree JSONL despite the auto-import opt-out. After that, ordinary cwd discovery selects this local DB; filesystem inodes differ. --no-auto-import does not prevent missing-DB recovery. A35–A41.
- These observations assume ordinary .beads discovery, default metadata and no explicit redirect/BEADS_DIR/cache overrides; they are not a claim about every supported br configuration.
- In this repository, Hive's post-checkout hook explicitly targets $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.beads/beads.db. show-toplevel means the current worktree, not Honeycomb's canonical root. The missing-DB helper branch uses --no-auto-import sync --merge --force-jsonl, creating a local DB during honeycomb add. Git traces verified real post-checkout execution. Hive therefore normally has ONE DATABASE PER WORKTREE, despite upstream br's DB-less-worktree fallback. B21–B25, C17.

### Visibility and reconciliation

- Hive config disables both sync.auto_import and sync.auto_flush. A worktree create remains DB-only: neither JSONL nor main's DB sees it. Worktree br sync --merge exports/reconciles only that worktree; main JSONL remained SHA-256-identical and main's DB still lacked the bead. B28–B34.
- The pre-commit Beads step exports/reconciles and stages worktree JSONL; commit carries it. Git merge transports the JSONL to main; post-merge reconciles main's DB, making the change visible even with auto-import disabled. Reverse visibility requires the analogous main export + commit + worktree merge/reconciliation. Hooks reconcile the current checkout; they do not replicate databases or transport branch state themselves. B35–B52.
- A DB-only addition and an independent JSONL-only label edit both survived the pre-commit sync, commit and merge, without forced conflict resolution. B53–B66. The disposable pre-commit wrapper retained only unchanged beads-sync --stage; unrelated lint-staged/typecheck steps were intentionally omitted. Real post-checkout/post-merge and beads-sync were copied unchanged; copied Husky dispatch attached them to Git's lifecycle. No custom merge driver was needed for the tested nonconflicting transports; divergent JSONL Git conflicts were outside this spike, not claimed as tested.
- Without Hive hooks, explicit JSONL transport via flush + commit + merge still works, but a recipient with --no-auto-import reads its old DB; a default br read then auto-imports the changed recipient JSONL. A48–A65.
- Claiming the seed task in canonical DB left its worktree copy open; the identical ID could then be claimed successfully in the worktree DB too. Separate stores are independent coordination domains, not a repository-wide claim lock. C14–C15 prove independent claims, not single-DB atomicity (that is the installed br contract/source).

### Explicit canonical BEADS_DB/--db

- BEADS_DB=<canonical>/.beads/beads.db from an initialized worktree selects canonical DB, project config and sibling canonical JSONL. A pinned create is visible immediately to main's DB, not the worktree's private DB. With Hive config, neither JSONL auto-flushes; pinned sync --merge writes ONLY canonical JSONL. C01–C05.
- With vanilla defaults, the same pin auto-flushes canonical JSONL only. Even malformed worktree JSONL is irrelevant to the pinned family's freshness check. D01–D02. No redirect file or redirected_from output was necessary for explicit routing in these fixtures.
- Existing Hive beads-sync supplies its own --db <worktree path>, which wins over inherited BEADS_DB. Giving a bee canonical BEADS_DB therefore DOES NOT switch current hooks to a shared database policy. C06. Furthermore git add <canonical>/.beads/issues.jsonl from a linked worktree fails exit 128, outside repository: canonical export cannot simply be staged by a worktree's current pre-commit. C16.
- Replacing canonical JSONL with an older worktree generation is NOT a safe additive handoff. In C07, sync --merge retained an active pending canonical title update and an active worktree-only addition, but TOMBSTONED the already-exported canonical-only bead omitted by the older JSONL (delete_reason="merge deletion"). Missing-from-JSONL relative to the base is interpreted as deletion. C07/C07b now assert status as well as title; the earlier title-only check missed this and was corrected after review. Do not blindly copy stale worktree JSONL over a shared tracker; coherent base/transport policy is required. This also does not promise conflict-free same-field edits.
- Absolute --db under .beads works from a neutral, nonrepository cwd for main, worktree-local and another unrelated repository. Colony need not have a repo-specific process cwd to route br. C08–C10.
- --db wins over BEADS_DB and legacy aliases. Inherited BD_DB/BD_DATABASE can override BEADS_DB alone; the launch boundary must remove competing database/JSONL/directory/cache overrides, or explicitly route command-owned br calls. C11–C13. Pin the whole workspace family, not an external cache DB with incidental caller config.

### Freshness and --allow-stale

- On a clean default DB, changed CANONICAL JSONL is auto-imported before a pinned read. --allow-stale and --no-auto-import instead return the old DB view. D03–D05. These flags are not worktree-sharing mechanisms.
- Dirty DB plus externally changed JSONL is not an automatic hard refusal in this installed version: startup WARNs "Skipping auto-import", returns exit 0 and the old DB view. Explicit sync --merge reconciled independent pending changes after establishing the common base. D06–D07.
- --allow-stale sync --flush-only still refused loss of a JSONL-only ID: exit 7, CONFIG_ERROR, "Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues". Explicit merge retained it. D08–D09. --allow-stale sync --merge also refused a conflicting title edit: exit 7, CONFIG_ERROR, BothModified. It does not bypass export guards or select a conflict winner. D10.
- Missing beads.base.jsonl with differing DB/JSONL refuses to guess an ancestor (exit 6, SYNC_CONFLICT). E01–E03 explicitly retain this fixture/result: a DB-only seed plus empty JSONL refused merge; initial flush-only followed by merge established agreement and a base. Normal Hive missing-DB bootstrap already explicitly chooses JSONL. Auto-import does not itself advance the three-way merge base: checkpoint agreement with sync --merge when needed. In an earlier retained refinement run, skipping that checkpoint led to BothModified when another JSONL title generation was presented; this is not an argument to force routine sync.
- br's mutation success does not guarantee JSONL publication: Hive intentionally disables it; default auto-flush failures may warn after the DB mutation. Poll the selected DB using br, not issues.jsonl as a live queue. Do not use --allow-stale/--force as a blanket daemon error workaround; surface sync conflicts for reconciliation.

### Recommendation for the epic/spec (not applied)

Recommend ONE CANONICAL TRACKER PER REPOSITORY for bee/colony runtime, while preserving caller/worktree cwd for code execution. Set a bee's BEADS_DB to the absolute canonical .beads/beads.db; use explicit --db for colony/bee-owned br calls. This separates execution location from coordination authority. Canonical here is Honeycomb's primary root (or the Git common-directory equivalent), not git rev-parse --show-toplevel in a worktree.

Why prefer this over ct's cwd-only preference: Hive creates private stores, so a main-only daemon cannot observe a worktree's new spawn, task claims or closure until commit/merge. A parent waiting for its queued child cannot rely on that handoff. Polling every worktree DB can make cwd-local spawning visible, but it still allows independent claims of identical task IDs across stores and duplicates imported spawn records. That alternative is viable only if the spec intentionally defines independent workspace queues and registers/pins each caller's resolved br where database; it is not interchangeable with one repository-wide queue. The evidence justifies recommending canonical authority, not silently changing today's policy.

System-wide colony should maintain explicit repository registrations keyed by canonical root, with that repo's absolute database path and bees.toml/config location. Poll each registered endpoint through a subprocess-scoped br --db <path>, and persist that endpoint with each admitted spawn/bee. Use a separate execution cwd for each bee. Never infer a target from colony's own cwd or set process-global BEADS_DB/chdir across repositories. All br show/ready/claim/status/close calls for a spawn and its tasks must use the same authority. The neutral-cwd, two-repo probes establish routing feasibility; registry implementation, daemon concurrency, recovery and dynamic repository enrollment belong to the downstream design, not this spike.

### Required follow-ups if adopting the recommendation

1. Explicitly approve/document the tracker authority in AGENTS.md and the bee/colony spec: worktree code cwd remains allowed/required; br mutations for runtime tasks use the canonical repo tracker. No policy file was changed by this spike.
2. Revisit .husky/beads-sync and prepare/post-checkout/pre-commit/post-merge integration together, including how canonical JSONL is transported/staged for a worktree commit. Merely exporting BEADS_DB or replacing the helper's DB path is insufficient; it currently creates local stores and stages checkout-local JSONL. C07b demonstrates that replaying an older checkout JSONL over canonical JSONL can tombstone newer canonical records. Do not invent a canonical-db/local-jsonl hybrid or blind snapshot-copy migration without checking br's family/path safety and establishing the correct merge ancestor.
3. Reconcile extant worktree DB-only state before changing authority; setting the env var alone would abandon pending local claims/notes. Define synchronization and semantic-conflict handling without routine force/stale bypasses. Preserve current Hive auto-sync configuration unless a deliberate follow-up changes it.
4. Specify canonical root resolution, repository registration, per-spawn database pinning and environment sanitization at the bee/colony boundary. If ct chooses workspace-local queues instead, require polling registered workspace DBs (not main only) and an explicit task/spawn identity/claim-domain rule.

No follow-up bead was created or claimed; these are handoff requirements for the already-blocked downstream design/spec work.
