Read governing AGENTS.md, lib/colony/AGENTS.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, architecture.md, domain.md and GLOSSARY.md; no docs/adr directory exists in this checkout. Applied codebase-design, robustness and TypeScript review guidance. Read complete hv-x6q7 and shared consultation hv-rnpw. Original user words are coordinator-recorded quotations, not independently recovered transcript: “we also only need the ranking to handle contention right? its not actually something we need most of the time”; “or does it get used for all spawns?”; “yes lets do that, so dispatch the work to handle both issues, one to change *when* we rank and one to minimise our ranking to readonly rather than this whole copy waste thing”. The accepted goal is contention-only ranking; the exact priority-group algorithm is the implementing task's design, consistent with the librarian proposal in hv-rnpw.

Verdict: aligned; no architectural code changes required in the examined diff.

1. Ownership, seam and depth
Architecture Package responsibilities and seams plus lib/colony/AGENTS.md assign scheduling and dispatch to Colony, claims/retries/settlement to the request machine, persistence to Store, and shared contracts only to Shared. dispatch.ts:149-181 coordinates priority groups inside the existing pass. scheduler.ts:50-63 adds one pure hasContention predicate and reuses hasCapacity/capacityConstraints for every dimension. No new cross-package imports, generic scheduling module, persistent state, timer, cache, or hypothetical injected interface appears. The existing pageRanks(repository, state, taskIds) seam and ranking.ts are unchanged, preserving sibling hv-hj1p's independent scope. I/O remains at the existing Colony effect seams; scheduler stays pure.

2. Admission meaning and monotone capacity
Dispatch reads the actual refreshed inventory once (dispatch.ts:155-158; store.ts:81-104) and retains starting/running attempts. Numeric native priority groups are visited in increasing urgency value (159-160). Feasibility is evaluated against actual occupied slots (161-163). hasContention tentatively appends only individually feasible occupants and reuses the same colony, effective kind override, and launch-bucket limits (scheduler.ts:55-81). Because those constraints are additive upper bounds, this joint-fit test is order independent: failure means not all feasible candidates can fit, not that a different planner is required. Empty, lone, saturated, zero-capacity, and all-fit sets skip PageRank; FIFO always skips it. A blocked kind or bucket does not suppress unrelated feasible requests. A contended group uses the existing priority/maximum-linked-task PageRank/FIFO/ID comparator (dispatch.ts:188-212; scheduler.ts:30-36). Infeasible candidates still reach the existing capacity-wait observation path (dispatch.ts:176,270-272).

This is narrow enough: the projected list is a disposable fit calculation, never a claim plan or launch authority. It does not search subsets or optimize utilization. PageRank is called separately for each contended priority group; the optional one-map-per-pass reuse proposed in hv-rnpw was not implemented. That is acceptable within the preserved seam and no-cache scope; it is not a new policy violation.

3. Claims, actual reservations and non-preemption
The authoritative sequence is still hasCapacity -> claimRequest -> durable reserve -> occupied.push -> receipt/supervisor/verified permission (dispatch.ts:223-259). Store.reserve atomically inserts the starting attempt and advances its request to executing (store.ts:196-210). Occupancy changes only after a successful reservation. acquireRequest returns null after a claim conflict or all-tasks-closed settlement (request.ts:252-290); partial claims are released through the existing ownership-checked settlement path (request.ts:441-479; claims.ts:48-80). Consequently a failed high-priority claim leaves room for lower-priority candidates, whose contention is calculated afterward, not against hypothetical success. Unexpected I/O errors still abort visibly rather than trigger a scheduling fallback. No stop/eviction path was added; retained occupants continue to count when maxima shrink, satisfying README Scheduling and hv-x6q7's explicit no-preemption requirement. Normal request and label reconciliation still precedes admission (dispatch.ts:74-77).

4. Failure timing is intentionally non-atomic
An uncontended higher-priority launch can finish its handoff before a lower-priority group calls PageRank. If that ranking fails, dispatch.ts:173-175 leaves the repository operation at dispatch.rank; history.ts:154-157 retains the failed operation and rethrows; colony.ts:40-51 moves the colony to failed. Earlier launches retain their executing request/starting attempt checkpoint, receipt and separate completed launch evidence (dispatch.ts:229-266; store.ts:196-210). They are neither silently rolled back nor relaunched in the failed pass. This is the consequence explicitly discussed in hv-rnpw, consistent with detached supervision and durable checkpoints in architecture.md Authority and persistence. No claim is acquired for the failing group before its ranking completes. No swallowed error or implicit FIFO fallback exists.

Stale/incomplete documentation, separate from code divergence
README Scheduling at lib/colony/README.md:379 still describes same-tier PageRank without the newly accepted contention gate. docs/architecture.md request-flow picture remains a coarse prepare/rank/claim sequence. Proposed narrow curation follow-up: qualify README's scheduling paragraph so PageRank is required only for individually feasible same-priority requests that cannot jointly fit remaining colony/kind/worktree capacity, and state that earlier successful group launches remain when a later ranking fails. The sibling's read-source wording can be coordinated in that same paragraph. This review does not authorize or perform the edit. There is no need for a new ADR or scheduler framework from this observation alone.

Verification and limits
Accepted supplied evidence: hv-bm12 reports full bun run check passed, with smoke extension still in progress at delegation. I inspected the new predicate cases and real-process scheduler smoke diff, including actual BV call counting, all-fit/saturated behavior, priority/capacity scenarios, FIFO and a surfaced ranker failure. I did not run quality suites in this advisory role. Higher-priority partial-claim failure leaving lower-tier contention, and a later-tier rank error after an earlier launch, were traced through the implementation; no runtime evidence for those combined cases was supplied. Existing retry.smoke.test.ts contains partial-claim coverage but I did not rerun it. No sibling hv-hj1p implementation or final merged branch was reviewed. You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

title: AFK prototype: build Bee and Colony end to end
description:
# Independent AFK prototype: build Bee and Colony end to end

## Mandate and isolation

This is a parallel, experimental build epic authorized by ct after the 2026-10-04 architecture grilling. Build a working prototype start-to-finish in an autonomous agent loop; it might be suitable to ship, but shipping is not assumed. This is NOT another design/HITL phase. The agent is delegated ordinary implementation choices, command naming, small schema decisions and prototype tradeoffs. Make a concrete choice, record it with evidence, and keep progressing rather than asking ct to bikeshed every detail.

The original hv-3x8 epic and ALL its descendants are read-only reference material. Do not claim, update, close, reparent, relabel or add dependency/related edges to those records. This prototype has its own top-level epic, features and implementation tasks and no prerequisite on the original plan. Read the current section of hv-3x8.9.1 and the source dialogue hv-3x8.17 as context only; this epic freezes the prototype contract and explicitly supplies defaults for previously open questions. Do not replay superseded proposals from the transcript. Do not treat success here as completing the original epic.

Use a dedicated nested Honeycomb worktree and prototype branch. Implement in sensible existing/new package locations after consulting the librarian; do not dump a second application into scripts or invent a parallel framework. Preserve current only-@hive/shared cross-package boundaries. Changes to main, production services, installed user harness configuration or original tracker work are not part of this authorization. The prototype may alter code in its isolated branch, but must not retire the existing worker loop, native agent definitions or hooks merely because the original plan contemplated that later. No automatic merge, release, Homebrew publication or deployment.

Scope is the complete Bee/Colony request/configuration/dispatch/daemon/scheduling/recovery/inspection path, including launcher-provided identity and native harness launch profiles. Standalone Scent/native-session hook rollout is orthogonal and remains out of scope; supplied identity must work without it. No GUI, cron service, model-price accounting, minimum worker population, compatibility shims or speculative capability/plugin framework.

## Mandatory build style: useful vertical slices and libraries

1. Work in small usable slices. The first launches one bee from a manually created spawn bead with no daemon or Bee CLI. For each slice define its cli.ts command/flag/help/JSON surface before implementing that path. Do not first scaffold the entire CLI, all packages, all types or a universal service framework.
2. Lean on maintained libraries where they fit. Consult current authoritative docs and existing repo patterns before building equivalent machinery. Commander for command parsing, existing schemas/Zod, Bun.TOML and Bun SQLite are natural starting points; use the repo's existing tools where appropriate. An ORM is not mandatory merely because there is SQLite.
3. As soon as there are multiple meaningful discriminated unions to branch over, use ts-pattern for exhaustive matching. Do not accumulate parallel switch ladders or avoid the library through casts and optional fields. This prototype will cross that threshold in its request/command/launch results, so adopt it in the first meaningful contracts, not as a later cleanup promise.
4. As soon as lifecycle/state transitions exceed a couple of simple cases, use XState. This prototype's awake/asleep plus request/attempt/retry/recovery behavior crosses that threshold. Introduce an actual XState model with the daemon/lifecycle slice rather than a growing collection of booleans, timers and ad hoc transition reducers. A token import or a dead demonstration machine does not satisfy this directive.
5. Use a popular existing template engine and its normal language, not handwritten substitution or a new DSL. Handlebars is the researched default candidate: strict missing values, no HTML escaping for argv, eager syntax validation at config load because compile() is lazy. Verify its current documented API and a tiny runtime probe; another established tool is acceptable if a concrete mismatch warrants it. Execute executable + argument tokens without a shell command string. No unrestricted shell evaluation hidden inside recipe templating.
6. Fail loudly for invalid config, missing named formulas, unsupported invocation parameters and ownership ambiguity. Do not silently invent values, fall back to another model/harness, swallow failures or build a production-grade recovery framework for hypothetical cases.

## Product contract frozen for this prototype

- A system-wide daemon hosts one event loop per registered repository (a colony). A bee is the running agent; its spawn bead is a request. A task bead is the work. Identity/Actor/Owner/Assignee remain distinct.
- Bee reads canonical-root bees.toml recipe/kind defaults, applies explicit recipe flags such as --model, --effort and --harness, and snapshots the effective values in a spawn bead. No alternate Bee --config file, worktree-first lookup or runtime daemon dependency. Bee may submit while server/colony is down or asleep.
- Colony loads canonical configuration on wake and applies the current named harness formula to the captured recipe. Kind defaults and caps are distinct from executable/argv formulas keyed by harness name. Bee may name a harness installed only via a Colony formula override; the two sides do not auto-synchronize.
- Default execution cwd is the canonical worktree. Explicit --cwd may be any existing directory and changes execution location only, not configuration discovery or the selected tracker. Persist explicit per-repository/per-attempt BEADS_DB authority; never route by the daemon's own cwd or mutate global environment when switching repositories.
- Spawn classification is separate exact-match labels system, bee, agent:<kind>, with related task links and supplied/minted friendly assignee. Snapshot recipe data structurally, not as shell strings stuffed into labels. Spawn creation does not claim task beads. Preserve human-reservation and duplicate-open-request refusals; blocked tasks may wait.
- Colony init creates config; wake/sleep control colony activity; explicit add/remove manage registry membership; daemon commands are separate. Use tmux-like lazy default server startup and explicit socket/server targeting. CLI names beyond those meanings may be chosen by the builder and documented.
- Nothing happens in a sleeping colony: no request polling, launch, retry or closure reconciliation. Detached bees continue. On wake reconcile closed requests as well as open ones: do not relaunch a closed request, and stop a known surviving execution whose request closed, then release its unfinished claims.
- Durable awake registrations recover after daemon restart; sleeping registrations stay asleep. wake --temp lasts only until explicit sleep/remove or daemon exit and is not restored. No queue-empty/idle auto-expiry. A fresh wake, including recovery wake, re-reads canonical configuration rather than restoring transient formula/limit overrides.
- Canonical configuration is the durable baseline. Colony SQLite may hold active formula/limit overrides, NOT recipe-default overrides, and immutable history. Reset/wake drops active overrides, not their audit trail. Request values do not change, but a later template can change a retry's actual invocation. Record spawn/recipe identity, actual formula revision, actual executable/argv and attempt outcome; requested/source formula identity is not proof of execution identity.
- Attribution for CLI config changes should reuse explicit actor/environment conventions; do not fabricate who authored a manually edited file. Logs live outside Beads. Minimal last-observed request summaries may be written for Bee status, with timestamps/freshness; do not promise live daemon state from Beads.
- No min. Use non-preemptive per-kind and per-colony maxima, with the scoped execution-location cap below. Reducing 20 to 18 leaves all existing workers alive; new launch eligibility resumes at count 17. Do not infer monetary cost from model names.
- All remaining open linked tasks must be ready; closed tasks satisfy the request. All tasks closed means close request without launching. Highest urgency among related task beads wins capacity (P0 ahead of P1); use existing BV ranking for same-priority work if a complete usable ranking interface can be obtained, not a new homemade graph ranker.
- Crashes can retry within a configured budget. Confirm the old owned execution stopped before clearing its own unfinished task claims; replacement reclaims them using the same spawn-friendly identity. Cancellation/exhaustion closes the request and releases only its own unfinished claims. Do not infer provider success solely from process exit code if the request remains unfinished.

## Concrete AFK defaults for previously open details

These are prototype decisions, not changes to the original epic. The builder may replace a choice when a real smoke demonstrates a problem, provided the reason, changed contract and regression receipt are recorded in this prototype's notes/docs.

- Start with max_retries = 3 additional attempts after the first. Count each unfinished unexpected exit against the budget; no elaborate progress-based reset rule. Select/document a small bounded retry delay through configuration and keep delay tests deterministic. No retries while asleep.
- If a multi-task claim fails, stop that request rather than inventing partial-work scheduling; after its execution stops release only the tasks this execution actually claimed. A task reserved for a human after submission, or claimed by another agent, keeps the request waiting with a visible reason. Never steal or clear someone else's claim.
- Registry membership and wake state are distinct: sleeping durable entries remain discoverable; remove forgets future scheduling but does not delete config/Beads data or kill unrelated processes. Existing owned executions still have their attempt records; the CLI must expose that they can outlive registration. Re-add/wake can reconcile them without duplicate launch.
- Per-worktree capacity uses the worktree containing the recorded launch cwd, or canonicalized external cwd when it is not in a worktree. Capture that bucket at dispatch; do not chase later process chdir or automatically-created worktrees. Canonical-default launches therefore share the canonical bucket. Scope the colony-wide total per registered repository; a server-global budget is not required initially.
- BV investigation must not stall the build. Prefer a verified complete score source for eligible task IDs and aggregate by best ranked linked task within a native-priority tier. Known triage output can be top-10 only. If no complete contract is available, use explicitly documented FIFO (request creation time, then ID) within the priority tier, expose that mode, and retain the limitation in the final report. Do not treat missing BV scores as proof of lowest rank or silently change a configured ranking mode after an error.
- For argv/model/prompt fields, use the chosen library's normal syntax and strict failure behavior. Names/schema details are delegated; no need to ask ct about every spelling. Unknown recipe fields, missing values and invalid configured formulas must have a small explicit boundary contract, not silent guessing.
- Use requested kind labels for caps and actual formula/attempt records for execution history. Select simple final outcome names and a Beads-visible status projection while implementing; do not revive retired reap/ancestry terms from old proposals. Beads-only status describes the request and recorded observations; Colony status inspects the actual runtime.

## Verification: real, small disposable smokes are the main evidence

The user explicitly authorizes small smoke tests against real disposable repositories, SQLite databases, br processes, OS processes and local sockets. This is not permission to use Hive's working tracker or the user's default daemon as test fixtures.

- Create throwaway Git projects and real br/Colony SQLite databases for each scenario, with explicit test endpoints and private socket/state directories. Use a canonical checkout plus linked worktrees for routing tests. The live Hive BEADS_DB remains only for implementation tracking; pass separate explicit endpoint/env to every smoke child so inherited state cannot leak.
- Build only small reusable setup/teardown helpers using existing test patterns. Do not replace br/SQLite/process APIs with giant fake services, and do not create a general-purpose testing framework. Real local scripted harness processes are useful deterministic fixtures but must be identified as fixtures, never claimed as real native-agent conformance.
- Prefer observable CLI outputs, database rows, files, child tool-environment receipts, exit events and log records. Wait on observable conditions with bounded deadlines; avoid arbitrary sleeps, wall-clock races and long monolithic scenarios. Clean up only processes/socket paths/directories owned by the smoke; retain useful failure artifacts and never kill unrelated work.
- Some focused unit tests are appropriate for pure priority/normalization/template boundaries and lifecycle assertions. Do not chase coverage or duplicate schema/library guarantees. Keep slow/provider probes separately selectable from fast unit/integration runs.

Do not install accounts, change user hook trust, disable production safeguards or run unbounded provider jobs. Missing credentials/binaries are genuine evidenced external blockers, not reasons to fake a pass. Continue independent local slices, leave required unverified acceptance unchecked, and report what is needed.

Full bun run check plus changed-code/appropriate broader suites are gates; follow the repository's test lock and review workflow. Final integration reruns the small smoke scenarios from clean state and verifies teardown.

## Agent-loop execution contract

Read this epic before every child task. Work only inside this prototype subtree: select an unblocked open leaf task, inspect it, claim with your harness actor and owner ct, sync, implement in the dedicated worktree, verify, append evidence, close and sync. Parent ownership is not a child claim. Respect existing reservations. Close a feature only when its children and feature-level smoke outcomes are complete, then continue to the next feature. Do not stop just because the first demo works, and do not select unrelated ready work outside this subtree.

All prototype work is AFK-eligible: no hitl label or human assignment gates are planned. Missing product details should be resolved conservatively under this directive, with a recorded prototype decision, rather than sent back as a new grilling round. Genuine external blockers, tracker sync conflicts, unsafe process ownership, missing credentials or new destructive scope still require an honest stop/report; autonomy is not permission to force them. Do not close blocked/unverified acceptance as done or hide it with a substitute fixture.

At completion leave a reviewable prototype branch, concise user usage/demo instructions, command/API reference, architecture and schema notes sufficient to continue, and evidence for all runnable scenarios. title: Consult on scoped asynchronous Busy Bee reviews
description: Read-only follow-up consultation to hv-osmg; review that prior report for context. User explicitly changes direction: "use waggle as inspiration but don’t use it, rebuild what you need in a new lib or even directly in a workflow". Latest request in context: user is unsure whether review belongs on Bee CLI or in a dedicated Busy Bee workflow. Wants an agent to submit a file/glob, HEAD, a commit SHA, or explicit Git diff range; software collects actual Git/file evidence, deterministically matches known globs to specialist concerns, creates separate review task beads and bees, and returns results. Use cases: review a file just finished while coding; review only commit six after commits one through five were reviewed; review PR content through an explicit diff range, without PR convenience for now. User asks: "do we need a separate thing? Do we need a busy bee status or something so that it can know when the work has completed and it can move on to the next engine step?" User called the Git-gathering layer "the workflow engine"; do not silently accept or dismiss placement, explain the smallest fit with current architecture. No implementation or documentation edits authorized in this consultation. Prior advice: workflow policy remains repo-owned, no Waggle product dependency; Busy Bee automatic dispatch currently overrides kind prompt; existing change-review example has dynamic actors and one editor but agent-authored input fingerprints. Relevant files: lib/busybee/README.md, SPEC.md, src/runtime.ts, src/definition.ts, docs/busybee-workflows.md, example change-review. Focus: (1) smallest concrete I/O seam to let one user-facing invocation accept simple scopes and produce deterministic frozen evidence under CURRENT engine contracts (no shell/Git in pure chart callbacks); distinguish existing capability from needed generic preparation or CLI seam; (2) show vs collect vs wait/report semantics and what a parent workflow would need; (3) immutable snapshot necessity if caller continues editing, commit vs worktree/range semantics; (4) where new helper code belongs, avoiding a new product lib absent a real need. Return compact evidence-backed recommendation and unresolved user decisions on this delivery task; do not create implementation or curation work. No need for broad tracker search or live classification. Prior sync-lock issue has cleared; coordinating agent successfully ran beads:sync at start of this turn.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Deliver read-only advice distinguishing current Busy Bee commands from minimal proposed preparation, review result and continuation additions.
notes:
LATEST USER CORRECTION — overrides the snapshot discussion in the original brief. User says: "> keep working while it reviews\nyes this is on the calling agent to manage, they can work on X while bees review Y\nif they decide to work on X while X is under review that’s on them" and then "i don’t want to handle that in engine". Settled scope: no engine-managed snapshots, worktree isolation, locks, drift detection or review invalidation for concurrent edits. The calling agent owns non-interference. Workflow resolves requested Git/file scope, deterministically matches concerns, spawns bees and collects results using caller-selected checkout. Ordinary Git ref resolution/provenance is still scope selection, not concurrency safety. Reflect this supplied rationale in advice; do not reintroduce isolation as a requirement. No documentation/implementation edits authorized.
Consultation delivered 2026-10-09 — mode: consult, read-only targets. Inspected revision c15e7fad6e4fab74cc5a825a9bfe1e0298a38fde (clean checkout), delivery task hv-gc0n, prior report hv-osmg. Supplied Colony actor green-moral-leopon owns this delivery task. Original user words supplied in hv-gc0n: “use waggle as inspiration but don’t use it, rebuild what you need in a new lib or even directly in a workflow”; “do we need a separate thing? Do we need a busy bee status or something so that it can know when the work has completed and it can move on to the next engine step?” Other scope details are the coordinating agent's description, not a direct transcript. No implementation, documentation or evidence-record writes are authorized.

Recommendation
Use a dedicated repository review workflow plus a small executable preparation adapter beside it. Busy Bee projects and advances the chart; the adapter resolves scope and freezes Git/file evidence; the workflow deterministically routes specialist concerns; Bee/Colony execute review tasks. Do not add a Bee review command, a Waggle dependency, or a new product library for this one consumer. A single user-facing invocation is possible with the current engine by wrapping preparation + busybee run. A pure workflow module alone cannot supply the required Git I/O under today's contract.

1. Evidence and reuse
- docs/architecture.md (package responsibilities, authority and persistence) and lib/busybee/SPEC.md settle ownership: XState owns progression, Beads owns work, Colony owns execution. Shared needs actual cross-product consumers; review policy is not one.
- docs/busybee-workflows.md:9–17 and :58–80 require pure workflow actions and task callbacks that render frozen briefs. lib/busybee/src/definition.ts:48–62 has no preparation/effect hook. runtime.ts:229–268 reads already-supplied JSON and starts the machine. Services.execute/readText/readBytes in native.ts:52–79 are existing injected I/O seams inside the runner, not dependencies passed to author callbacks. Trusted Bun imports are executable but are not permission to perform Git work at import time or inside chart actions.
- examples/change-review/workflow.ts:130–228 already supplies dynamic reviewer actors, separate task briefs, result schemas and a join. Its planner chooses jobs and authors a revision string; lines 340–357 only compare that string. It does not gather or authenticate evidence. Its repair loop (:241–287) assumes review-round editing stops and then grants one repair worker edit authority. Reuse its fan-out/join pattern, not that planner or automatic repair policy for this request.
- runtime.ts:530–583 collects closed automatic tasks' JSON notes, validates them and advances; accepted payloads enter private history at :513–523. RunView (:91–96, :895–909) exposes active tasks, created visits and machine status, not accepted history or an aggregate report.
- Important continuing constraint: runtime.ts:861–891 sends --prompt and fixes --cwd to endpoint.repo. producer.ts:169–193 and colony/README.md:96 confirm that --prompt replaces kind instructions. bee.kind currently selects execution defaults without preserving the specialist prompt. Metadata supports kind only, not a separate per-task execution directory.
- Existing integration tests at lib/busybee/tests/integration/native.test.ts:135–213 inspect revision mismatch, repair navigation and concurrent scripted collection. They are evidence of intended existing contracts, not a live snapshot review demonstration; I did not run them.

2. Smallest concrete submission seam — proposed new paths
Propose .workflows/review/workflow.ts, busybee.toml, and submit.ts (executable I/O adapter); add scope.ts only if it hides substantial scope/snapshot work. These are proposed files, not present today. A command such as “bun .workflows/review/submit.ts --commit HEAD” or “--files 'lib/busybee/src/*.ts'” can be one user-facing invocation. It should:
(a) parse an explicit scope variant; (b) resolve refs / expand quoted globs through injected Git/filesystem operations; (c) capture the actual evidence and an immutable manifest; (d) compute stable concern matches from captured paths; (e) write prepared workflow input outside the fingerprinted workflow folder; (f) invoke existing busybee run review --input-file ... --repo REVIEW_CHECKOUT --db ORIGINAL_DB --owner ct, retaining actor identity; (g) return run ID, resolved scope, snapshot ID, coverage and task/request IDs promptly.
Use a retained Honeycomb-managed review worktree for a full contextual checkout when needed, with the unchanged named workflow available there. Preserve tracker selection independently. Starting the review run in that checkout makes current dispatch's fixed cwd correct without adding per-task cwd metadata. Continue show/collect against an unchanged definition and retain review material until consumers finish.
Keep concern selection pure and deterministic. Match normalized paths, including old and new paths for renames and old paths for deletions; retain all matching concerns and group them into sensible briefs. Freeze the selected concern/source references and matched files. Report uncovered files instead of treating no match as approval. Existing skills remain standards authority; the prior proposed concern index under .agents/skills/code-review/ can hold routing references, not duplicated standards. No Waggle execution or LLM classifier is required.
If the required spelling is specifically busybee run review with raw simple scope input and no wrapper, that DOES need an engine change: a one-shot preparation seam invoked by run/start before pure initialization. Specify raw/prepared schemas, injected capabilities, persisted prepared input and error behavior; never re-run capture on show, discover, collect or restore. Keep validate's pure contract explicit. Do not build a general effect-node system just to obtain Git input. The wrapper is the smaller initial design; a reusable preparation contract is a proposal, not existing functionality.

3. Scope and snapshot semantics — proposed defaults requiring agreement
- Files/globs: review the selected files' captured current contents; tracked and nonignored untracked files can participate. Decide explicitly if the desired meaning is instead “only changes in those files since a base.” Do not infer that from a path string.
- Commit C (including --commit HEAD): review the change introduced by C, against its parent, using C's tree for context. Resolve HEAD once. Thus commit six reviews C5..C6, while earlier code remains context rather than newly reviewed changes. Require an explicit base for ambiguous merge comparisons; define root-commit behavior.
- Explicit range A..B: compare the resolved endpoint trees. If supporting A...B, explicitly resolve merge-base(A,B)..B and retain that distinction. An explicit range supplies PR content without fetching PR metadata. None of these committed scopes silently includes worktree edits.
At submission, store scope kind, resolved revisions/base, sorted path/status manifest, before/after contents or retrievable pinned blobs, patch, and a content digest. Freeze relevant surrounding source and guidance too; a copied patch plus live surrounding files is insufficient if the caller continues editing. For uncommitted contents, capture bytes during a brief stable capture window; fail visibly if observed files change during capture. Editing may resume after submission confirms the snapshot. Do not promise an atomic filesystem snapshot merely because a digest exists.
Reviewers consume the preserved material; results carry the snapshot ID and concern ID. Match those IDs on acceptance. A hash identifies bytes; it does not preserve them. Later edits do not invalidate a completed review of its original snapshot, but that review is not approval of the newer work. A landing/parent acceptance step must compare against the intended scope again. No durable “already reviewed through commit five” registry is needed for explicit per-commit requests.

4. Status, collection, results and continuation
- Existing show RUN is the read-only status operation. It restores saved machine state and reports status/active/created; it neither ingests closed results nor proves a worker is alive. A new status synonym is unnecessary.
- Existing collect RUN is a mutation: process currently closed automatic tasks, validate payloads, send events, publish the next frontier. A single call can spawn the next automatic stage. It does not block for open workers, continuously drive future stages, aggregate a public final report, or inspect failed Bee requests. Task closure is not approval, and Colony finishing is not chart advancement.
- Small proposed result addition: expose accepted result history (or a defined final machine output) through a public read-only Busy Bee operation. A workflow-local formatter can then return coverage, findings, evidence and the snapshot receipt without scraping system checkpoints. Today a caller can follow created[].bead and read task notes, but there is no generic public accepted-results response. Prefer accepted checkpoint payloads for durable reporting, not later mutable notes.
- Optional wait/report convenience is a driver loop around collect and inspection, not another scheduler. It needs explicit terminal conditions: completed report, manual work needing input, failed/blocked request with unfinished work, malformed result/engine error, and timeout. Timeout leaves the run pending; it must not imply approval, cancellation or retry. Do not retry partial_effects or steal a checkpoint lock. Keep a long wait outside the checkpoint lock. No autonomous continuation survives the driver's exit under current contracts.
Make this review workflow finish with a report even when findings exist; the initiating editor handles fixes and can submit another scope. Separate execution/progress from review verdict. Preserve Standards and Spec axes; lacking a spec is explicit missing coverage, not a pass.

Parent workflow:
Within one chart, the existing child actors/sendParent join can advance the parent's next state when a caller collects results. It does not need to call status from a guard. But fresh Git capture when reaching a later review stage still needs an external I/O step, and today's fixed execution cwd makes an independent snapshot review run especially useful.
For a separately started child review run, the parent needs a persisted child run ID + snapshot ID, a public report contract, and a coordinator/bridge that drives the child and submits the resulting parent outcome. With current contracts that can be a parent worker invoking the deterministic submit helper, recording the child ID, waiting/collecting, then writing its parent task's JSON result and closing it; the normal parent collector advances the parent. There is no built-in durable child-run invocation or notification bridge. Prefer an existing caller/process over spawning a bee just to poll, and account for a waiting Colony worker retaining capacity. If unattended advancement after every caller exits is required, that is a separate driver-lifecycle decision; adding show/status cannot provide it.

5. Trade-offs and unresolved decisions
The wrapper adds one small entrypoint, but preserves pure charts and avoids teaching Busy Bee or Bee Git-review policy. A generic preparation hook gives cleaner common CLI syntax at the cost of a new engine contract; adopt it only if that interface is required. A retained snapshot costs storage but is necessary for asynchronous evidence fidelity. Reuse current fan-out/collection and existing Git commands; the inspected Shared/Tooling/Honeycomb alternatives handle process execution or worktree/tracker maintenance, not this scope-evidence contract.
Before implementation settle: file-content versus file-diff semantics; commit/merge/range conventions; exact concern catalogue and unmatched-file behavior; spec source; result retention; caller-driven versus unattended continuation. Preserve specialist prompts by moving Busy Bee's result/closure instructions onto the task brief and retaining kind instructions, without changing Bee's --prompt replacement meaning. That generic dispatch change is needed even with the wrapper. No new library, automatic repair loop, review cache or daemon is justified by the supplied request.

Proposed architectural-friction entry — NOT filed
- architectural-friction: 2026-10-09; topic scoped-review-preparation-and-continuation; where deterministic evidence capture and asynchronous completion fit around Busy Bee.
- Interpretation: user calls Git gathering “the workflow engine” and asks whether status is needed. Existing workflow domain ownership fits, but pure chart contracts do not expose native preparation; show is observation, collect is progression, and neither is a durable driver.
- Resolution: user explicitly rejects a Waggle dependency. Remaining placement/interface proposals above await acceptance; no supplied rationale beyond the quoted direction, and no implementation outcome.
- Guidance gap: missing concrete recipe for deterministic native preparation + frozen inputs and parent/child result continuation; no contradiction in the existing pure-action rule. Prior hv-osmg advice to keep I/O outside callbacks was insufficiently concrete for a one-command scope interface.
- Action/outcome: propose workflow-local submit adapter, preserved evidence, explicit result/driver contracts and prompt delivery correction. No curation writes.
- Evidence: hv-gc0n quoted correction and questions, hv-osmg prior advice, revision and file pointers above. Sample limited to these two related consultations and current source; no recurrence claim or broad historical search.

Verification/scope: source and supplied task history inspected; no code, docs, workflows, labels or implementation beads changed. No quality suites run for this read-only consultation. Startup beads:sync succeeded; only this delivery task is updated/closed, then synchronized before bee finish.
Coordinator disposition after reading delivered report: the snapshot/isolation recommendations in that report were superseded by the user correction recorded above before report delivery. They are NOT accepted requirements. No retained review worktree, immutable evidence manifest, snapshot ID acceptance gate, stable capture window, concurrent-edit detection, landing freshness gate, or engine-managed invalidation is part of this design. Caller explicitly owns same-scope concurrency. Retain only the workflow-local submission/helper placement, deterministic routing, separate report/completion semantics, and existing show/collect findings as proposals. Ordinary resolved Git refs and selected paths suffice for scope provenance; do not treat this consultation as authorization to build a snapshot subsystem. Documentation/evidence curation remains unauthorized.
close_reason: Completed: read-only consultation verified in notes against c15e7fad6e4fab74cc5a825a9bfe1e0298a38fde; concrete scope preparation and snapshot proposal, current show/collect limits, result and parent-continuation additions, prompt constraint and unresolved decisions delivered.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.

Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. title: honeycomb: move wk wrapper behaviour into the engine (simplify; focus follows humans, never agents)
description:
Move worktree lifecycle behaviour out of the Nushell `wk` wrapper (`lib/honeycomb/nu/honeycomb/`, ~475 lines) into the honeycomb engine, leaving the shell layer as a thin alias whose only irreducible job is changing the calling shell's cwd.

This is a simplification. `wk` works well today; the goal is to move the same behaviour into TypeScript and delete duplication, not to add new safety machinery.

## What moves

- Post-create setup and its rollback (today: wrapper runs the script, then rolls back via the `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK` backdoor and a raw `git branch -f`).
- tmux open/switch/close and session naming (already emitted as `session.name`).
- The fzf worktree picker.
- `--self` resolution and human status lines.

The pool-full recycle picker already exists in the engine (`pickFullPoolSlot`); the wrapper only reimplemented it because it calls `--json`. The shim will call human mode, so it disappears for free.

## Focus follows the human, never the agent

One flag, `--interactive`, passed only by `wk`:

- **With it**: `add` opens and focuses the worktree's multiplexer session (or tells the shell to `cd` when not in a multiplexer); `remove`/`finish` close sessions for removed worktrees and send the shell to the canonical root if it was inside one.
- **Without it** (agents, scripts): no multiplexer calls and no cd directive at all. An agent can't steal focus or kill a session because it never touches sessions.

Terminal detection is deliberately not used: agents run inside the user's tmux panes and can have a PTY.

## Decisions

- `add` always runs setup in the engine. No deferred mode. `post_create_script_path` stays in JSON as always `null`.
- Multiplexer support is a small injected service (tmux first) so another multiplexer with a similar API could replace it.
- Shell cwd handoff: the engine writes a directory path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
- `remove --self` is a boolean (the worktree containing `--cwd`).
- JSON changes are additive only.

## End state

`mod.nu` is a ~30-line shim; `tmux.nu` is deleted.

Make `honeycomb add` always run post-create setup itself, and delete the wrapper's setup/rollback code and the backdoor it needed.

## Scope

- Run the setup command inside the existing rollback region in `src/commands/add.ts` (non-pooled and pooled paths), so the existing `rollbackNonPoolAdd` / `rollbackPooledAllocation` handle failure. On failure, fail with the setup error (blocked payload with a clear reason under `--json`).
- Run it the same way pool initialisation does (`src/application/pool.ts`, `HookRunner`). Drop the temp script file if running the command directly with `WK_ROOT`/`WK_CREATED` in the env is equivalent.
- Under `--json`, setup output goes to stderr so stdout stays a single JSON document.
- Keep `post_create_script_path` in the payload, always `null`.
- The wrapper's `run-post-create` and `rollback-add-payload` become dead code (they no-op on a null path): delete them, plus `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK`, `Deps.internalRollback`, `remove --skip-pre-remote-check` and its handling in `src/protocol.ts` / `src/commands/remove.ts`.
- Update CLI help and README text that tells callers to run `post_create_script_path`.

## Acceptance

- Tests: setup success; setup failure rolls back (new branch deleted, pre-existing branch restored, pool slot freed); `--json` stdout parses while setup prints output.

title: honeycomb: multiplexer service with tmux implementation
description:
Add a small multiplexer service with a tmux implementation, ported from `nu/honeycomb/tmux.nu` and the pane lookup in `pick-worktree`.

## Scope

- Interface (e.g. `src/integrations/multiplexer.ts`), intent-shaped and free of tmux syntax:
  - `open({ name, title, path })`: create the session if missing, then focus it;
  - `closeUnder(path)`: close sessions rooted at or below a path;

- `src/integrations/tmux.ts`: straight port of the wrapper's commands. Session names come from `sessionNameForWorktreePath`.
- Select tmux when `$TMUX` is set, otherwise a null implementation (so the caller falls back to the cd directive).

title: honeycomb: --interactive flag drives session open/close and cd directive
description:
Add the `--interactive` flag and wire the multiplexer and cd directive into `add`, `remove` and `finish`.

## Scope

- Global `--interactive` option, read after Commander parses and passed through `Deps` or dispatch.
- With `--interactive`:
  - `add`: `multiplexer.open(...)` for the new worktree; outside a multiplexer, write the worktree path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
  - `remove` / `finish` cleanup: if the shell's cwd was inside the removed worktree, write the canonical root to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`; then `multiplexer.closeUnder(path)` as the **last** step, after output is written (closing the invoking session may kill this process).
- Without `--interactive`: no multiplexer calls, no cd file.
- tmux failures are a warning on stderr; they never undo the git operation.
- Git already runs from `/` (`src/git/executor.ts`), so removing the worktree containing the process cwd needs no extra handling. Verify.

## Acceptance

- Fake-multiplexer tests: interactive add opens; non-interactive add/remove make no multiplexer calls; interactive remove writes the canonical root and closes sessions last.
notes:

Design: --interactive is a Commander global passed through args like --cwd (parseOptions boolean; finish allows it). Multiplexer gains readonly attached (tmux true, NoMultiplexer false).
